previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent epigastric pain and vomiting, previously attributed to pancreatitis but now under question, was admitted for symptom management and diagnostic evaluation. Initial workup revealed only a mildly elevated lipase and normal imaging, casting doubt on pancreatitis. A HIDA scan showed normal gallbladder ejection fraction, ruling out biliary dyskinesia. The clinical team, in consultation with her gastroenterologist, concluded her symptoms were likely due to an intestinal motility disorder with visceral hypersensitivity. Her diet was advanced from NPO to clear liquids, then soft, and finally regular diet as symptoms improved. Pain and nausea were controlled with oral medications by discharge. She was discharged home with PRN Dilaudid and Prochlorperazine, continuation of psychiatric medications, and referral to a motility specialist for outpatient follow-up. Her mental health conditions remained stable throughout the admission.

___ old female with anxiety, Depression, PTSD,  recurrent 
epigastric abdominal pain of unclear etiology, although she does 
have intermittent elevations in lipase, these are felt to be

She has been hospitalized 55 times in the last ___ years at ___, 
and 14 times in the past 12 months.  She was diagnosed in ___ 
with sphincter of oddi dysfunction III by manometry, but this 
diagnosis has since fallen out of favor and is unlikely to be 
the cause of her symptoms. She has had 4 prior ERCPs -all 
normal, and numerous imaging studies (CT, MRI, US), also normal 
as well. She now presents with acute on chronic pain, nausea, 
vomiting,  and intermittent loose stool.

# ACUTE ON CHRONIC ABDOMINAL PAIN NOS: Kept NPO and gave IV 
hydration, pain control, and anti-emetics.  She is on multiple 
QT prolonging agents but QTc 411 on discharge.  Team was in 
communication with Dr. ___ who has a long-standing 
relationship with her, as well as Dr. ___ from ___. 
 

The ___ team documented the following from discussion with Dr. 
___ - ""Essentially he explained that over the years he has 
been unclear whether she has SOD, functional abdominal pain, or 
biliary dyskinesia. It seems fairly clear she doesnt have 
chronic pancreatitis. Recently he has been most concerned about 
her having biliary dyskinesia vs functional abdominal pain.  He 
recently performed a HIDA scan on her which showed a slightly 
depressed ejection fraction (~55%)  but certainly not below the 
40% we typically see in these cases. He says shes also had 
imaging studies that have shown gallstones in the past.  He also 
told me that she has just recently seen ___ at the 
___ who personally reviewed her case and did NOT feel as 
though there was an indication for cholecystectomy.""  Ultimately 
it was decided to support her through this hospitalization and 
have her follow-up with her outpatient providers this week.  

On discharge she was tolerating a regular diet and requiring 
minimal oral narcotics and anti-emetics.
